statute_title: Operating a Vehicle Under the Influence (OVI)
offense_class: 1st Degree Misdemeanor (first/second); 4th Degree Felony (third within 10 years); 3rd Degree Felony (fourth+ within 10 years)
elements: Defendant operated a vehicle, streetcar, or trackless trolley within Ohio
Defendant was under the influence of alcohol, a drug of abuse, or a combination
Defendant had a BAC of .08 or higher, or tested positive for a listed controlled substance
mandatory_minimum: 3 consecutive days in jail or 3-day Driver Intervention Program (first); 10 consecutive days (second within 10 years); 30 consecutive days (third within 10 years); 60 consecutive days (fourth within 10 years)
enhancements: High-tier BAC (.17 or above) — mandatory 6 days jail (first offense)
Refusal of chemical test — enhanced administrative suspension
Fourth or subsequent within 10 years (F3 felony)
notes: Ohio uses 'OVI' not 'DUI.' Administrative License Suspension (ALS) is separate from criminal penalties. Refusal = 1-year ALS; failure = 90-day ALS. Ignition interlock may be required. Driver Intervention Program can substitute for 3 days jail on first offense.

offense_class: 1st Degree Misdemeanor (first/second)
elements: Defendant operated a vehicle in Ohio
Defendant was under the influence of alcohol, drugs, or combination
Defendant refused to submit to a chemical test
mandatory_minimum: 3 consecutive days (first); 10 consecutive days (second within 10 years)
notes: Refusal triggers 1-year Administrative License Suspension. Refusal is admissible at trial. No per se BAC to prove but prosecution must still prove impairment. Limited driving privileges available after 30 days.

offense_class: 2nd Degree Felony; 1st Degree Felony (prior OVI conviction)
elements: Defendant operated a motor vehicle
Defendant caused the death of another
Defendant was operating under the influence of alcohol or drugs at the time
notes: Distinct from vehicular homicide (ORC § 2903.06(A)(2)) which requires recklessness without OVI element. Mandatory license suspension for life upon conviction.

offense_class: Unclassified Felony
penalty_max: Life imprisonment with parole eligibility after 15 years
elements: Defendant purposely caused the death of another
OR defendant caused the death of another as a proximate result of committing or attempting to commit a felony offense of violence
enhancements: Prior conviction for murder or aggravated murder
notes: Distinguished from aggravated murder (ORC § 2903.01) which requires prior calculation and design or specified circumstances. Murder carries 15-to-life; aggravated murder carries life without parole or death.

offense_class: 1st Degree Felony
elements: Defendant knowingly caused the death of another
Defendant acted under the influence of sudden passion or sudden fit of rage brought on by serious provocation by the victim
notes: Often charged as lesser-included offense of murder. Provocation must be by the victim and sufficient to provoke a reasonable person. Heat of passion must not have cooled.

offense_class: 1st Degree Felony (during felony); 3rd Degree Felony (during misdemeanor)
elements: Defendant caused the death of another
The death was caused as a proximate result of committing or attempting to commit a felony or misdemeanor
enhancements: Underlying offense was a felony of violence
Victim was a child or elderly person
notes: No intent to kill required. Degree depends on the underlying offense. Proximate cause must be established between the unlawful act and death.

offense_class: 2nd Degree Felony; 1st Degree Felony (victim is peace officer/firefighter on duty)
elements: Defendant knowingly caused serious physical harm to another
OR defendant knowingly caused or attempted to cause physical harm to another by means of a deadly weapon or dangerous ordnance
mandatory_minimum: Mandatory prison term if firearm specification
enhancements: Victim is peace officer, firefighter, or BCII investigator on duty (elevates to F1)
notes: Two prongs: (1) serious physical harm or (2) deadly weapon. Serious physical harm includes risk of death, permanent disfigurement, or prolonged impairment. Mandatory prison for F2 felonious assault.

offense_class: 1st Degree Misdemeanor; 5th Degree Felony (victim is peace officer, teacher, health worker, etc.)
elements: Defendant knowingly caused or attempted to cause physical harm to another
OR defendant recklessly caused serious physical harm to another
enhancements: Victim is peace officer, firefighter, BCI investigator on duty (F5)
Victim is school teacher or administrator (F5)
Prior assault conviction against same type of victim (F4)
notes: Simple assault is M1. Elevates to F5 when victim is a protected class on duty. 'Knowingly' means defendant was aware conduct would probably cause physical harm. 'Recklessly' for serious harm prong.

offense_class: 1st Degree Misdemeanor (first); 4th or 3rd Degree Felony (repeat offenses)
elements: Defendant knowingly caused or attempted to cause physical harm to a family or household member
OR defendant recklessly caused serious physical harm to a family or household member
OR defendant threatened force or violence against a family or household member by a threat of force
enhancements: One prior DV or related conviction (F4)
Two or more prior DV or related convictions (F3)
Prior conviction for violence against same family member
notes: Family or household member includes spouse, former spouse, parent, child, person living together, or person who has a child in common. Conviction triggers federal firearms prohibition. CPO (civil protection order) is separate civil remedy.

offense_class: 4th Degree Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant knowingly caused another to believe that the defendant would cause physical harm to the person or property of the other person
Or a member of the other person's immediate family or household
notes: Threat of harm — no physical contact required. Distinguished from aggravated menacing (ORC § 2903.21) which involves threats of serious physical harm and is an M1 or F5.

offense_class: 1st Degree Felony; 2nd Degree Felony (if victim released unharmed in safe place)
elements: Defendant by force, threat, or deception removed another from the place where found
OR restrained the liberty of another person
For the purpose of holding for ransom, facilitating a felony or flight, terrorizing, engaging in sexual activity, or hindering a governmental function
notes: Reduced to F2 if victim is released unharmed in a safe place. Kidnapping merges with underlying felony in some circumstances per State v. Logan. Allied offense analysis required.

offense_class: 1st Degree Felony
elements: Defendant engaged in sexual conduct with another person
The sexual conduct was by force or threat of force
OR the victim's ability to resist or consent was substantially impaired due to mental or physical condition or age
mandatory_minimum: 5 years (if defendant drugged victim); 25 years to life (if victim under 10); 15 years to life (if victim under 13)
enhancements: Defendant administered controlled substance surreptitiously (minimum 5 years)
notes: Sexual conduct includes vaginal, anal, and oral intercourse and cunnilingus. Spousal rape is a crime in Ohio. Conviction requires sex offender registration (Tier III lifetime). Defendant may be subject to indefinite prison term under Reagan Tokes Law.

offense_class: 3rd Degree Felony; 2nd Degree Felony (victim under 13)
elements: Defendant engaged in sexual conduct with another person who was not the defendant's spouse
Defendant knew the other person's ability to resist was substantially impaired
OR defendant held a position of authority over the victim (teacher, coach, clergy, etc.)
notes: Distinct from rape — sexual battery involves coercion through position of authority or impairment without force. Requires sex offender registration. Position of authority includes teacher, coach, clergy, therapist, correctional officer.

offense_class: 4th Degree Felony; 3rd Degree Felony (victim under 13)
elements: Defendant had sexual contact with another person
By force or threat of force
OR victim's ability to resist was substantially impaired
OR victim was under 13
notes: Sexual contact means touching for sexual arousal (less than sexual conduct). Analogous to forcible fondling. Requires sex offender registration (Tier I or II depending on circumstances).

offense_class: 2nd Degree Felony (force/threat used); 3rd Degree Felony (no force threat)
elements: Defendant in attempting or committing a theft offense or fleeing immediately after
Had a deadly weapon on or about the defendant's person or under the defendant's control
OR inflicted, attempted, or threatened physical harm to another
OR used or threatened immediate use of force against another
notes: F2 if defendant inflicted/threatened/attempted harm or had a deadly weapon. F3 if force or threat of force used without weapon or harm. Distinguished from aggravated robbery (ORC § 2911.01) which involves deadly weapon display or serious physical harm.

offense_class: 1st Degree Felony
elements: Defendant in attempting or committing a theft offense or fleeing immediately after
Had a deadly weapon on or about the defendant's person or under the defendant's control and either displayed, brandished, indicated possession of, or used it
OR inflicted or attempted to inflict serious physical harm on another
mandatory_minimum: Mandatory prison term; 3-year mandatory consecutive for firearm specification
notes: Most serious robbery offense in Ohio. Mandatory prison — community control not available. Firearm specification adds mandatory consecutive time. Armed robbery of financial institution often charged under this statute.

offense_class: 2nd Degree Felony (occupied structure, person present); 3rd Degree Felony (occupied structure); 4th Degree Felony
elements: Defendant trespassed in an occupied structure or separately secured portion
With purpose to commit a criminal offense therein
OR defendant trespassed in a permanent or temporary habitation when any person was present or likely to be present
enhancements: Person present in structure (elevates to F2)
notes: F2 if person present or likely present; F3 if occupied structure with no one present; F4 for other burglary. Distinguished from aggravated burglary (ORC § 2911.11) which involves weapon or harm. 'Occupied structure' means any structure used for overnight accommodation, business, or storage.

offense_class: 1st Degree Felony
elements: Defendant trespassed in an occupied structure when another person (not accomplice) was present
With purpose to commit any criminal offense
AND defendant had a deadly weapon or dangerous ordnance, OR inflicted or attempted to inflict physical harm on another
notes: Highest-level burglary offense. Requires both presence of another person AND weapon or infliction of harm. Mandatory prison — no community control.

offense_class: 4th Degree Misdemeanor; 1st Degree Misdemeanor (certain habitations or critical infrastructure)
elements: Defendant knowingly entered or remained on the land or premises of another
Without privilege, by force, stealth, deception, or by violating clearly posted notices or explicit warnings
notes: M4 for standard trespass. Elevates to M1 for habitation trespass, certain agricultural, or critical infrastructure properties. Commonly charged as lesser-included of burglary.

offense_class: 1st Degree Misdemeanor (under $1,000); 5th Degree Felony ($1,000-$7,500); 4th Degree Felony ($7,500-$150,000); 3rd Degree Felony ($150,000-$750,000); 2nd Degree Felony ($750,000+)
elements: Defendant knowingly obtained or exerted control over the property or services of another
Without the consent of the owner or person authorized to give consent
With the purpose to deprive the owner of the property or services
enhancements: Victim is elderly or disabled (penalty one degree higher)
Motor vehicle theft (F4 minimum regardless of value)
Firearm theft (F3 minimum regardless of value)
notes: Value of property determines offense level. Elderly/disabled victim bumps penalty one degree. Theft of motor vehicle is minimum F4. Theft of firearm is minimum F3. Theft of a dangerous drug is F4.

offense_class: 1st Degree Misdemeanor
elements: Defendant knowingly obtained or exerted control over property of another
Without consent and with purpose to deprive
Value of property is less than $1,000
enhancements: Elderly or disabled victim (elevates to F5)
notes: Most common shoplifting charge. Repeat offenses can be elevated. Civil demand for restitution from retailer is separate from criminal prosecution.

offense_class: 4th Degree Felony ($7,500-$150,000); 3rd Degree Felony ($150,000-$750,000); 2nd Degree Felony ($750,000+)
elements: Defendant knowingly obtained or exerted control over property of another
Without consent and with purpose to deprive
Value of property exceeds $7,500
notes: Grand theft is theft at higher value thresholds. Auto theft is always at least F4 even if vehicle value is low. Restitution commonly ordered.

offense_class: 5th Degree Felony; higher degrees based on value/victim
elements: Defendant without consent of the other person used, obtained, or possessed personal identifying information of another
With the intent to fraudulently obtain credit, property, services, or employment
OR to avoid criminal prosecution
enhancements: Victim is elderly or disabled (one degree higher)
Value thresholds (F5 base; escalates with amount)
notes: Personal identifying information includes SSN, driver's license, bank account, credit card numbers. Federal charges possible if interstate commerce involved.

offense_class: 5th Degree Felony
elements: Defendant with purpose to defraud or knowing that the defendant is facilitating a fraud
Forged any writing of another without authority
OR forged any writing purporting to be genuine when it was actually spurious
OR uttered or possessed with purpose to utter any forged writing
enhancements: Forged instrument is a government document
notes: Covers checks, deeds, wills, contracts, and other writings. 'Uttering' means presenting or using a forged document. Often charged alongside theft and identity fraud.

offense_class: 1st Degree Misdemeanor (under $1,000); escalates by value same as theft
penalty_max: 180 days (M1); 12 months (F5); up to 8 years (F2) based on value
elements: Defendant received, retained, or disposed of property of another
Knowing or having reasonable cause to believe the property had been obtained through the commission of a theft offense
notes: Knowledge or reasonable cause to believe property was stolen is required. Value thresholds match theft offense escalation. Often charged alongside theft.

offense_class: Varies by schedule and amount: Minor Misdemeanor to 1st Degree Felony
penalty_max: 11 years (F1 for large amounts of Schedule I/II)
elements: Defendant knowingly obtained, possessed, or used a controlled substance
mandatory_minimum: Varies; mandatory prison for bulk amounts of certain drugs
notes: Penalty depends on drug schedule and amount. Marijuana under 100g is minor misdemeanor (no jail, $150 fine). Fentanyl and heroin possession carries enhanced penalties. Ohio has a pre-trial diversion program for first-time low-level offenders.

offense_class: Minor Misdemeanor (under 100g); 4th Degree Misdemeanor (100-200g); 5th Degree Felony (200g-1kg); escalates by amount
elements: Defendant knowingly obtained, possessed, or used marijuana
notes: Under 100g is a minor misdemeanor — fine only, no jail, no criminal record if first offense. Ohio legalized recreational marijuana in 2023 (Issue 2) for adults 21+ up to 2.5 oz. Possession limits differ from pre-2023 thresholds.

offense_class: 4th or 5th Degree Felony (small amounts); up to 1st Degree Felony (major drug offender)
penalty_max: 11 years (F1); mandatory prison for bulk amounts
elements: Defendant knowingly sold or offered to sell a controlled substance
OR prepared for shipment, shipped, transported, delivered, prepared for distribution, or distributed a controlled substance
With knowledge or reasonable cause to believe it would be sold
mandatory_minimum: Mandatory prison for bulk amounts; major drug offender specification adds mandatory 11 years
enhancements: Near school or juvenile (one degree higher)
Major drug offender (mandatory maximum prison term)
notes: Trafficking does not require an actual sale — offering to sell, transporting with intent, or preparation for distribution all qualify. Degree depends on schedule and amount of drug.

offense_class: 4th Degree Misdemeanor (possession); 2nd Degree Misdemeanor (sale/delivery)
elements: Defendant knowingly used or possessed with purpose to use drug paraphernalia
OR sold, delivered, or manufactured with intent to sell drug paraphernalia
enhancements: Sale to a minor (one degree higher)
notes: Drug paraphernalia includes pipes, syringes (with certain exceptions), bongs, rolling papers when combined with other evidence of drug use. Needle exchange programs provide limited immunity.

offense_class: 1st Degree Felony (risk to person); 2nd Degree Felony (occupied structure)
elements: Defendant by means of fire or explosion knowingly created a substantial risk of serious physical harm to any person other than the defendant
OR caused physical harm to any occupied structure
notes: Aggravated arson is the most serious fire-related offense. Lesser offenses include arson (ORC § 2909.03, F4) and criminal mischief. Fire set in connection with insurance fraud is common aggravating factor.

offense_class: 3rd Degree Felony
elements: Defendant knowingly acquired, had, carried, or used a firearm or dangerous ordnance
While under one of the listed disabilities: fugitive from justice, under indictment for or convicted of a felony of violence, drug offense, etc.
notes: Disabilities include: felony conviction involving violence, drug offenses, adjudicated mentally incompetent, chronic alcoholic, fugitive from justice, under indictment. Federal parallel charge under 18 USC § 922(g).

offense_class: 4th Degree Felony (without permit, non-qualifying); 1st Degree Misdemeanor (certain violations)
elements: Defendant knowingly carried or had concealed on the defendant's person or within reach
A handgun, deadly weapon, or dangerous ordnance
Without a valid concealed handgun license when required
enhancements: Prior conviction for offense of violence
notes: Ohio enacted constitutional carry (permitless carry) effective June 13, 2022 (SB 215). Adults 21+ who are not prohibited persons can carry concealed without a license. This significantly narrowed who can be charged. Still a crime for prohibited persons.

statute_title: Improperly Handling Firearms in a Motor Vehicle
offense_class: 4th Degree Felony (loaded, accessible); 1st Degree Misdemeanor (other violations)
elements: Defendant knowingly transported or had a loaded firearm in a motor vehicle
In a manner accessible to the operator or any passenger without leaving the vehicle
notes: Constitutional carry (SB 215, eff. 6/13/2022) changed the legal landscape. Lawful adults 21+ may have loaded handgun accessible in vehicle. Violations now mainly apply to prohibited persons or long guns.

offense_class: Minor Misdemeanor; 4th Degree Misdemeanor (persists after warning)
elements: Defendant recklessly caused inconvenience, annoyance, or alarm to another
By engaging in fighting, threatening harm, making unreasonable noise, or hindering movement of others
OR offensive conduct or language in public tending to provoke a violent response
enhancements: Persisting after reasonable warning or request to desist (elevates to M4)
notes: Most common public order offense. Alcohol-related disorderly conduct is frequently charged at bars, events, and college campuses. Often offered as plea deal from more serious charges.

statute_title: Failure to Comply with Order or Signal of Police Officer
offense_class: 1st Degree Misdemeanor (failure to comply with order); 4th Degree Felony (fleeing); 3rd Degree Felony (aggravated circumstances)
elements: Defendant failed to comply with a lawful order or signal of a police officer
OR defendant operated a motor vehicle so as to willfully elude or flee a police officer after receiving a visible or audible signal to stop
enhancements: Fleeing immediately after committing a felony (F3)
Operation caused substantial risk of serious physical harm (F3)
notes: Division (A) is mere failure to comply (M1). Division (B) involves fleeing in a vehicle (F4 or F3). Court must impose a class 2 license suspension. Often charged alongside other offenses arising from the pursuit.

offense_class: 2nd Degree Misdemeanor; 5th Degree Felony (if creates risk of physical harm)
elements: Defendant without privilege to do so and with purpose to prevent, obstruct, or delay the performance by a public official of any authorized act within the official's capacity
Did an act that hampered or impeded the public official in the performance of the official's lawful duties
enhancements: Creates risk of physical harm to any person (F5)
notes: Commonly charged alongside resisting arrest. Does not require physical force. Providing false information to an officer can constitute obstruction. Passive resistance (going limp, etc.) may or may not qualify depending on circumstances.

offense_class: 1st Degree Misdemeanor (general); 5th, 4th, or 3rd Degree Felony (in certain contexts)
penalty_max: 180 days (M1); up to 60 months (F3 in certain contexts)
elements: Defendant knowingly made a false statement or swore or affirmed the truth of a false statement previously made
When the statement is made in an official proceeding, to a law enforcement officer, on a government application, or in writing
enhancements: False claim of an emergency (F3 if serious harm results)
notes: Covers lying to police, filing false police reports, and false statements on government forms. Distinguished from perjury (ORC § 2921.11) which requires sworn testimony.

offense_class: 1st Degree Misdemeanor; 5th Degree Felony (prior conviction or threat of violence)
elements: Defendant knowingly made or caused a telecommunication or used a telecommunication facility
To make a threat of physical harm, to harass, to abuse, or to annoy another person
notes: Covers phone calls, texts, emails, and social media communications. Closely related to menacing by stalking (ORC § 2903.211). Frequently charged in domestic violence contexts.

offense_class: 1st Degree Misdemeanor; 4th Degree Felony (prior conviction or pattern of conduct; 5th Degree Felony (trespass)
elements: Defendant by engaging in a pattern of conduct knowingly caused another person to believe the defendant would cause physical harm to the other person or a family member
OR caused mental distress to the other person or a family member
enhancements: Prior conviction for menacing by stalking (F4)
Made threat while in violation of protection order (F4)
Trespass on victim's property as part of pattern (F5)
notes: Pattern of conduct means two or more actions or incidents closely related in time. Includes surveillance, following, monitoring, and electronic tracking. CPO violation enhances penalty.

offense_class: 1st Degree Misdemeanor (general); 3rd, 2nd, or 1st Degree Felony (serious harm, drug exposure, torture)
elements: Defendant being a parent, guardian, custodian, or person having custody of a child under 18
Created a substantial risk to the health or safety of the child by violating a duty of care, protection, or support
OR abused the child
enhancements: Serious physical harm to child (F2 or F1)
Administration of drug of abuse to child (F2 or F1)
notes: Commonly charged in drug cases where children are present. Methamphetamine lab exposure is automatic felony. Failure to provide adequate food, shelter, or medical care can constitute endangering.

offense_class: 1st Degree Misdemeanor; 5th Degree Felony (prior violation or with violence); 3rd Degree Felony (with serious harm)
elements: Defendant recklessly violated the terms of a protection order, consent agreement, or anti-stalking order issued pursuant to Ohio law or substantially equivalent order from another state
enhancements: Serious physical harm to protected person (F3)
notes: Applies to CPOs, TPOs, and consent agreements. Contact includes phone calls, texts, social media, and third-party contact. First violation is M1 but escalates quickly with priors.

statute_title: Intimidation of Attorney, Victim, or Witness
offense_class: 3rd Degree Felony
elements: Defendant knowingly attempted to intimidate or hinder the attendance or testimony of a witness, victim, or attorney in a criminal case or delinquency proceeding
OR attempted to influence, corrupt, or prevent the testimony of such person by force, threat, or intimidation
enhancements: Threat against family member of witness
notes: Also covers intimidation or retaliation against witnesses who have already testified. Closely related to retaliation (ORC § 2921.05).

offense_class: 5th Degree Felony (under $7,500); 4th Degree Felony ($7,500-$150,000); 3rd Degree Felony ($150,000+)
elements: Defendant knowingly caused serious physical harm to an occupied structure, its contents, or the real property on which the structure is situated
OR to property of another that is used in a profession, business, trade, or occupation, government property, or a place of worship
enhancements: Government property or place of worship
notes: Vandalism is always a felony in Ohio — the degree depends on value. This distinguishes it from criminal damaging/endangering (ORC § 2909.06) which is a M2 for lower-value damage.

offense_class: 2nd Degree Misdemeanor; 1st Degree Misdemeanor (occupied structure)
elements: Defendant knowingly caused or created a substantial risk of physical harm to any property of another
Without the other person's consent
notes: The misdemeanor counterpart to vandalism. Commonly charged for property damage that doesn't rise to the 'serious physical harm' threshold required for vandalism.

offense_class: 3rd Degree Felony (OVI-related); 4th Degree Felony (reckless); 1st Degree Misdemeanor (negligent)
elements: Defendant operated a motor vehicle and caused serious physical harm to another person
While under the influence, operating recklessly, or operating negligently
notes: Three levels: OVI-related (F3), reckless (F4), and negligent (M1). Must cause serious physical harm — not just injury. License suspension mandatory.

statute_title: Driving Under Suspension or Without a License
offense_class: Unclassified Misdemeanor; 1st Degree Misdemeanor (OVI-related suspension)
elements: Defendant operated a motor vehicle on any street, highway, or property used by the public
While the defendant's license was suspended, revoked, or cancelled, or without ever having obtained a license
mandatory_minimum: 3 consecutive days jail if suspension was OVI-related
notes: Ohio consolidated many driving-under-suspension statutes into ORC Chapter 4510. OVI-related suspension carries mandatory minimum jail. BMV points accumulate.

offense_class: 4th Degree Felony; 3rd Degree Felony (aggravated circumstances)
elements: Defendant operated a motor vehicle
Defendant willfully eluded or fled a police officer after receiving a visible or audible signal to bring the vehicle to a stop
enhancements: Substantial risk of serious physical harm during pursuit (F3)
notes: Division (B) of the failure to comply statute specifically addresses vehicular fleeing. Mandatory class 2 license suspension. Commonly results in additional charges based on pursuit conduct.

offense_class: 3rd Degree Misdemeanor; 1st Degree Misdemeanor (near school or with prior); 5th Degree Felony (third offense)
elements: Defendant solicited another to engage in sexual activity for hire
OR engaged in conduct or communication inviting, requesting, or suggesting that another engage in sexual activity for hire
enhancements: Prior soliciting conviction (M1; then F5 on third+)
notes: Ohio has shifted enforcement focus to buyers and traffickers rather than persons engaged in prostitution. Human trafficking (ORC § 2905.32) carries severe penalties for those who compel prostitution.

offense_class: 1st Degree Misdemeanor (under $1,000); 5th Degree Felony ($1,000-$7,500); escalates by amount
elements: Defendant practiced deception for the purpose of procuring the issuance of a credit card
OR knowingly bought, sold, or received a credit card from anyone other than the issuer
OR used a credit card knowing it was expired, revoked, or obtained through theft
notes: Covers fraudulent applications, trafficking in stolen cards, and unauthorized use. Often charged alongside identity fraud and theft. Value determines felony level.

offense_class: 1st Degree Misdemeanor (under $1,000); escalates by value
elements: Defendant with purpose to defraud issued or transferred or caused to be issued or transferred a check or other negotiable instrument
Knowing that it would be dishonored (insufficient funds or closed account)
notes: Prosecution must prove knowledge that check would bounce. Failure to make good within 10 days of dishonor notice creates a prima facie case of intent. Bank notification is key evidence.

offense_class: 3rd Degree Felony (from prison/detention); 5th Degree Felony (from supervision); 2nd Degree Felony (with violence)
elements: Defendant knowing the defendant is under detention or being reckless in that regard
Purposely broke or attempted to break the detention
OR purposely failed to return to detention after being granted temporary leave
enhancements: Use of physical force or threat (F2)
notes: Detention includes arrest, confinement in correctional facility, hospitalization, extradition, or supervision under community control. Failure to report to jail on scheduled date can constitute escape.

offense_class: Not a separate criminal offense — violation of conditions of existing sentence
penalty_max: Remaining prison term for underlying offense (up to original maximum sentence)
elements: Defendant was placed on community control sanctions as part of a criminal sentence
Defendant violated one or more conditions of community control (failed drug test, missed appointment, new arrest, absconding, etc.)
notes: Probation violations are heard by the sentencing judge. Standard of proof is preponderance of evidence (lower than beyond reasonable doubt). Court may extend supervision, add conditions, or impose prison sentence up to the remaining time. Technical violations treated differently than new criminal conduct.

offense_class: 3rd Degree Felony
elements: Defendant with purpose to obtain anything of value or induce another to do an unlawful act
Threatened to commit a specified offense or made a threat to expose matter tending to subject any person to hatred, contempt, or ridicule
OR to harm another's business reputation or personal reputation
notes: Extortion requires a threat to obtain something of value. Distinguished from robbery (immediate force). Blackmail falls under this statute. Threats to expose criminal activity, sexual conduct, or embarrassing information all qualify.

offense_class: 1st Degree Misdemeanor; 5th Degree Felony (elderly victim)
elements: Defendant knowingly used or operated an aircraft, motor vehicle, motorboat, or other motor-propelled vehicle
Without the consent of the owner or person authorized to give consent
notes: Distinct from theft — unauthorized use does not require intent to permanently deprive. Joyriding is the colloquial term. Commonly charged as lesser-included of motor vehicle theft.

offense_class: 3rd Degree Felony
elements: Defendant in any official proceeding knowingly made a false statement under oath or affirmation
OR made a statement that the defendant does not believe to be true under oath or affirmation relating to a material issue in an official proceeding
notes: Requires the statement to be material to the proceeding. Recantation defense exists if retraction occurs in the same proceeding before the false statement substantially affects the proceeding.

statute_title: Impersonation of a Peace Officer or Government Official
offense_class: 4th Degree Misdemeanor (general impersonation); 1st Degree Misdemeanor (commission of offense while impersonating); 3rd Degree Felony (arrest while impersonating)
elements: Defendant impersonated a peace officer, private police officer, or investigator of the bureau of criminal identification and investigation
OR impersonated an officer of a federal law enforcement agency
enhancements: Arresting or detaining someone while impersonating (F3)
notes: Wearing a fake uniform, displaying a fake badge, or verbally claiming to be an officer all qualify. Online impersonation may also be covered. F3 if defendant detains someone under pretense of authority.
